environmentalPersistence: Low to moderate — soil half-life ~1–30 days; degraded by specific caffeine-degrading bacteria; detected in most urban waterways globally

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Moderate — caffeine is allelopathic at moderate concentrations; inhibits cell division via phosphodiesterase-like effects
morphologicalEffects.wilting: Moderate — root inhibition reduces water uptake
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Mild to moderate — root tip necrosis at high doses
morphologicalEffects.pigmentation: Moderate — caffeine-induced anthocyanin documented; caffeine is itself an alkaloid produced as defense in coffee/tea plants — signals defense pathways
morphologicalEffects.rootGrowth: Moderately to strongly inhibited — allelopathic root inhibition well documented for caffeine
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: Root effects cause wilting across canopy; old leaves show chlorosis

molecularEffects.anthocyaninInduction: Moderate — caffeine triggers defense pathways via purine signaling

microbiomeEffects.beneficialBacteriaEffect: Moderately suppressed; caffeine-degrading bacteria (Pseudomonas, Rhodococcus) may dominate

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Green → moderate purple tint (anthocyanin) + chlorosis — similar to ibuprofen signature
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Moderate — theophylline/theobromine metabolite pattern; purine alkaloid signature distinctive

synergies.synergyNote: Coffee shop to wastewater to soil pipeline — caffeine, ibuprofen, and acetaminophen are co-detected in wastewater-irrigated fields globally; combined microbiome disruption is additive
synergies.antagonismNote: Caffeine is a purine analog; competes with cytokinin (also a purine derivative) for some signaling receptors — may partially reduce cytokinin anti-senescence effect

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Coffee, tea, energy drinks, soft drinks — most consumed psychoactive substance globally; excreted largely unchanged; detected in virtually all urban waterways and treated wastewater
educationalContext.classification: Stimulant alkaloid / pharmaceutical pollutant / natural allelopathic compound
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: Not intentionally applied as stressor — environmental contaminant; interestingly, coffee grounds (containing caffeine) are used as garden fertilizer and slug deterrent
educationalContext.humanToxicity: Low at typical consumption; toxic at very high doses (~150 mg/kg); no environmental risk to humans at detected concentrations
educationalContext.climateLink: Caffeine in water is an urban water quality indicator — its distribution maps human population density and is used as a pollution tracer
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Primarily environmental via wastewater; but coffee grounds applied as garden fertilizer introduce it directly to plant root zones
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: The most consumed drug in the world is polluting rivers and affecting plants — and you might be adding it to garden soil via coffee grounds. Immediately personal connection. Teachers and students both consume it daily.
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Pharmaceutical water pollution, caffeine as environmental tracer, coffee grounds as garden amendment
